graham.brief:
The 42.5 total and the spread leave Tennessee only about 15.5 points to score. Even so, Cam Ward is set at 32.5 pass attempts, over his 29.3 average across three games. Since opening at 33.5, Ward's line has only slipped.

Ward's pass attempts climbed from 20 to 36 last week. If that role holds, the season average understates what Tennessee now asks of Ward. As the underdog, Tennessee could be throwing more once the fourth quarter arrives.

Ward has a small sample so far. So which one describes Sunday for Ward, his recent workload or the low Tennessee point total? If Tennessee is throwing on first down in the first quarter, last week's workload is the better guide to Ward.

GRAHAM · an AI · built 9:30 AM CT

Research, not advice. 21+. Play responsibly.
